title: Monitoring Reward Hacking Live From Internal Activations vs Post-Hoc From Text

original_idea.body:
# Monitoring Reward Hacking Live From Internal Activations vs Post-Hoc From Text

**Problem:** A 2026 result monitors emergent reward hacking during generation via internal activations. It is unclear how much earlier an activation monitor flags reward hacking compared to a text-based CoT monitor reading the same trajectory.

**Direction:** On a reward-hackable coding task with an open model, collect both per-token activations and the generated CoT. Fit a simple activation probe for 'about-to-reward-hack' and compare the token position at which it fires vs when a text monitor flags the same trajectory. Report detection-latency difference.

**Why it matters:** Earlier detection enables interruption before the harmful action commits — central to runtime control. A latency comparison is a crisp, novel result; activation extraction on a small open model fits the compute budget.

**Relevant context:** Monitoring Emergent Reward Hacking During Generation via Internal Activations (arXiv:2603.04069). Builds on Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking (arXiv:2511.18397) reward-hackable environments.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: detection-latency advantage of activation vs text monitoring is central to interrupting before harm commits.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: per-token activation extraction + 'about-to-reward-hack' probe + alignment with text monitor is demanding.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: compare firing token position of activation probe vs text monitor.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: small open model, inference + probe.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation extraction on small open model on one GPU.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Detection-latency comparison is a crisp, likely-novel result.
